issues.legal_issue: A statutory power of suo motu revision that has no prescribed limitation period must be exercised within a reasonable time, assessed in context and on the facts of each case.
material_facts: The Collector initiated proceedings under the suo motu power about 13 to 15 years after validation certificates had been issued and cancelled them.
No convincing explanation was given for the delay.

In these appeals, fraud was not adequately pleaded with particulars or a date or period of discovery, and the argument that delay should run from discovery of fraud was not advanced before the High Court.

The affected landholders had relied on the certificates, and some had filed declarations under land-ceiling legislation on which orders had attained finality; later transfers and third-party rights could also be affected.
issues.conclusion: The words permitting action “at any time” do not authorize arbitrary or indefinite delay. The power must be exercised within a reasonable time, judged by the circumstances of the case; where fraud is involved, reasonable time runs from its detection or discovery. The High Court was right to set aside the cancellations made after the unexplained delay in these appeals.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 50-B(4) of the Andhra Pradesh (Telangana Area) Tenancy and Agricultural Lands Act, 1950, the absence of a specified limitation period does not make suo motu revision exercisable indefinitely. The words “at any time” must be construed contextually and reasonably, having regard to such matters as settled rights, third-party interests, subsequent bona fide transfers, and final orders under other legislation. In cases of fraud, the power may be exercised within a reasonable time from detection or discovery. The Court relied on D. Saibaba v. Bar Council of India and the principles of contextual statutory interpretation discussed in G.P. Singh’s Principles of Statutory Interpretation.

predicates.suo_motu_revision_proceeding: An authority is reviewing a subordinate official’s certificate or proceeding on its own initiative.
predicates.no_specific_limitation_period: The law authorizing the review does not prescribe a specific period within which the authority must act.

issues.definition: When an authority reviews a subordinate official’s decision on its own initiative and no specific time limit applies, its power is limited to action within a reasonable time.

issues.legal_issue: A transfer made before a later-enacted ceiling law does not become inconsistent with the earlier ceiling law expressly identified in the validation provision merely because it may affect the later law.
material_facts: The transactions in question took place in 1965, and possession was delivered at that time.
The validation applications were made within the extended period for applying.
The validation provision referred to inconsistency with the ceiling law enacted in 1961, while the law said to have been defeated came into force later.
The Collector cancelled validation certificates on the basis that the transactions defeated the later ceiling law.
issues.conclusion: The later ceiling law could not be substituted for the specific earlier law identified in the validation provision. The transactions could not have been made to defeat a law that came into force after they occurred, and the cancellation of the certificates was not justified on that ground.
issues.legal_principle: Section 50-B(1) and (2) of the Andhra Pradesh (Telangana Area) Tenancy and Agricultural Lands Act, 1950, governs validation of specified transfers; the reference to inconsistency with the ceiling law of 1961 is specific and cannot be read, through Section 18 of the Andhra Pradesh General Clauses Act, as referring instead to a later ceiling law. The Court agreed with the High Court’s interpretation and its conclusion that a transaction predating the later law could not have been made to defeat that law.

predicates.validation_certificate_cancellation_revi: A reviewing authority is considering whether to cancel a certificate validating a land transfer.
predicates.transfer_preceded_later_ceiling_law: The land transfer occurred before the ceiling law relied on as having been defeated came into force.
predicates.validation_test_identifies_earlier_ceili: The governing validation test expressly identifies an earlier ceiling law as the law with which the transfer must be consistent.

issues.definition: If a land transfer predates the later ceiling law and the validation test identifies an earlier ceiling law, the later law does not make the transfer inconsistent under that test.

issues.legal_issue: A finding that validation certificates were obtained by fraud may support cancellation when the authority acts within a reasonable time after discovery of the fraud.
material_facts: In these appeals, the High Court found that fraud in obtaining the validation certificates had been established on the material before it.
The High Court found that the authority acted within a reasonable time from discovering the fraud.
The Supreme Court found no valid ground to interfere with the High Court’s fact-based decision.
issues.conclusion: The Court upheld the cancellation of the validation certificates in these appeals and dismissed the appeals.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 50-B(4) of the Andhra Pradesh (Telangana Area) Tenancy and Agricultural Lands Act, 1950, suo motu review must be exercised within a reasonable time; where fraud is established, that period is assessed from its detection or discovery in light of the facts and circumstances. The Court accepted the High Court’s supported findings that fraud was established and that action was timely.

predicates.appeal_against_validation_cancellation: A party appeals against an order cancelling a certificate that validated a land transfer.
predicates.fraud_established: The evidence establishes that fraud was used to obtain the validation certificate.
predicates.action_within_reasonable_time_after_disc: The authority began and pursued the review within a reasonable time after the fraud was detected or discovered.

issues.definition: When an appeal challenges cancellation of a validation certificate, fraud is established, and the authority acted within a reasonable time after discovery, the cancellation is upheld.
